review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped downstream uses of iterateAmplitude/iterateAmplitudeSq. The file has no simp lemmas or attributes. Both definitions are nested `if`s, and the library repeatedly unfolds them by hand. I did not check whether `Real.rpow_natCast` or other existing simp rules would conflict with the proposed lemmas. I did not run Lean. I made no claim of loops or simp failures.

findings.excerpt: if i = 0 then 1 else if i ≤ 2 then η else η ^ ((i : ℝ) / 2)
findings.problem: The piecewise definition has no equation lemmas for its cases. These are `iterateAmplitude η 0 = 1`, `iterateAmplitude η 1 = η`, `iterateAmplitude η 2 = η`, and `iterateAmplitude η i = η ^ ((i:ℝ)/2)` for `3 ≤ i`. Downstream files fall back on `simp [iterateAmplitude]`, which unfolds the definition, or on `simp only [iterateAmplitude, ite_eq_right (by omega : ...), ...]` chains. They also prove the same `= η` facts again as local `have`s. The `i ≥ 3` case needs a hypothesis, so it works as a conditional rewrite lemma but not as a plain simp lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Add lemmas and tag the closed-numeral ones `@[simp]`: `iterateAmplitude_zero : iterateAmplitude η 0 = 1`, `iterateAmplitude_one : iterateAmplitude η 1 = η`, `iterateAmplitude_two : iterateAmplitude η 2 = η`. Add a conditional lemma `iterateAmplitude_of_three_le (h : 3 ≤ i) : iterateAmplitude η i = η ^ ((i:ℝ)/2)`, also marked `@[simp]`, since the side condition can be discharged by `omega`/`decide`. The users could then write `simp [iterateAmplitude_of_three_le h]`.
findings.benefit: Callers get a stable normal form for small indices instead of unfolding the `if` tree. This removes the repeated `ite_eq_right (by omega ...)` chains and local `h₁`/`h₂` re-proofs, and it keeps the `Finset.sum_range_succ` expansions in the downstream files readable.

evidence.excerpt: have h₁ : iterateAmplitude η 1 = η := by simp [iterateAmplitude]

findings.excerpt: if i = 0 then 1 else if i ≤ 2 then η ^ 2 else η ^ i
findings.problem: `iterateAmplitudeSq` also has no simp or equation lemmas for its cases. These are `Sq η 0 = 1`, `Sq η 1 = η^2`, `Sq η 2 = η^2`, and `Sq η i = η^i` for `3 ≤ i`. Both this file and later files redo the case analysis by hand. In this file, `iterateAmplitudeSq_previous` and `iterateAmplitudeSq_two_previous` use `norm_num [iterateAmplitudeSq]` and `simp only [iterateAmplitudeSq, ite_eq_right (by omega ...) ×4]`. `IteratesFiniteAnalyticSum` and `TLemmasAmplitude` use `simp [iterateAmplitudeSq, show ¬ k + 2 ≤ 2 by omega]`. Each call re-expands the definition and proves the same `if` conditions again.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] iterateAmplitudeSq_zero`, `iterateAmplitudeSq_one` and `iterateAmplitudeSq_two`, giving `1`, `η ^ 2` and `η ^ 2`. Add the conditional `iterateAmplitudeSq_of_three_le (h : 3 ≤ i) : iterateAmplitudeSq η i = η ^ i`. Then rewrite the four-`ite_eq_right` blocks as `rw [iterateAmplitudeSq_of_three_le (by omega), iterateAmplitudeSq_of_three_le (by omega)]`. Do not simp-tag the unfolded definition itself.
findings.benefit: Case-split proofs about the `i-1`/`i-2` recursions become short rewrites with an explicit normal form. Downstream `simp [iterateAmplitudeSq, ...]` calls stop depending on the exact shape of the nested `if`s.

evidence.excerpt: simp [iterateAmplitudeSq, show i ≠ 0 by omega, hi2]
